finding: Soot volume fraction of sooty attached flames several times greater in microgravity than in comparable normal-gravity flames
Dilution limits for methane and ethylene extended in microgravity (lifted flames at lower fuel concentrations)
Microgravity flames taller and wider than normal-gravity flames
Distinct peak in ion current at the most compact flame size in microgravity
Highly diluted flames stabilized with very weak fields; high field strengths produced corona and arc discharges
Flames self-extinguished below roughly 25 percent oxygen by volume
Radiative extinction at high flow rates and kinetic extinction at low flow rates; helium dilution shifted limits
Cool flames significantly smaller than corresponding hot flames
Microgravity suppresses buoyancy-driven flicker and gives spherical flames that simplify modeling
